newsitem.title: USA: One job, two chiefs in East St. Louis.
newsitem.headline: One job, two chiefs in East St. Louis.

text.p: For a time Tuesday East St. Louis had two police chiefs.

But Mayor Gordon Bush ended the confusion by announcing that he and other city officials were restoring Isadore Chambers to the chief's job he had held for more than eight years before he was demoted to sergeant by City Manager Lee Coleman.

The city manager said he took the action last week because he wanted new leadership and was upset over recent allegations of police brutality. He appointed the head of detectives, J.W. Cowan, as the new chief.
Chambers protested and both men reported for work for the same job Tuesday morning, 15 minutes apart.

The mayor, saying he was "bringing sanity to this insanity," announced after several hours of confusion and negotiations that he, the City Council and others were backing the old chief and that the city manager had agreed to work with Chambers.
